 © 2026 Yahoo. All rights reserved. For the second time in as many years, Kevin Kane will be paid well not to coach Purdue football's defense.
 Barry Odom fired Kane on Sunday only nine games into his second stint as the Boilermakers ' defensive coordinator. Per the employment contract released by the university, Kane is owed 100% of his remaining base salary through Dec. 31, 2027.
 Advertisement Advertisement Advertisement Kane will be paid $141,667 for November and December and the full $1 million owed for next season. His contract does not require the salary owed next season to be offset by whatever he makes at another job.
 Kane was previously fired in December 2024 with the rest of Ryan Walters' staff. He was owed $850,000 for the third and final year of that contract as defensive coordinator.
 Purdue pays Odom's 10 on-field assistants and strength coach a combined $6.3 million in 2026. It is unclear what the pool will be next season as five assistants have contracts which expire in December.
 From January: Why Barry Odom brought fired defensive coordinator back to Purdue football 
 Advertisement Advertisement Advertisement Odom is due a $5 million buyout if his contract is terminated prior to Dec. 31, and $4 million if fired after that date through Dec. 31, 2027.
